messages.subject: Discrete survival model specification
parts:
Hi everyone,


I am trying to run a multilevel survival model in brms, but my data is in person-period format (not person-time), e.g.:


 id      time      event    group     x1
  1       1          0        1       4
  1       2          0        1       3
  1       3          0        1       2
  1       4          0        1       1
  1       5          0        1       0
  1       6          1        1       3
  2       1          0        1       1
  2       2          0        1       0
  2       3          0        1       3
  2       4          0        1       2
  2       5          0        1       1
  2       6          1        1       0
  3       1          0        2       3
  3       2          0        2       2
  3       3          1        2       1
  4       1          0        2       2
  4       2          0        2       1
  4       3          0        2       0
  4       4          0        2       0


The brms documentation specifies a survival model on a dataset in person-time format:


## Survival regression modeling the time between the first
## and second recurrence of an infection in kidney patients.
fit3 <- brm(time | cens(censored) ~ age * sex + disease + (1|patient),
data = kidney, family = lognormal())


What would the brm model specification be for a discrete survival model on my data? I can imagine a logit with random intercept for id would look like:


fit <- brm(event ~ time + (1|id), data = data, family = 'bernoulli')


But how do I transform that into a discrete survival model?


Thanks!

messages.author: 6e3dd74b422c061b
messages.subject: Re: [brms-users] Discrete survival model specification
parts:
Hans Tierens made some recomendations in https://github.com/paul-buerkner/brms/issues/230.

I think your model is a special case of his model with with interval length being set to 1.
